svg.title: JavaScript 1.4 - this, Invocation and Object Model
svg.desc: One-page A4 infographic covering invocation and this, call apply bind, new, prototypes, property lookup, enumeration, creation approaches, descriptors, integrity levels, Proxy and Reflect.
svg.text: Print-first interview refresher | call site -> receiver -> property -> prototype -> invariant

g.text: Call site first. Definition site does not bind regular this.
Wrap it, or bind/store once for cleanup.
call/apply invoke now; bind returns a function. Bound args come first; later args append.
Re-bind keeps first this; new on a bound target uses a fresh this; call/apply/bind cannot replace arrow this.
Primitive return: ignored. Object/function return: replaces the fresh object.
Arrow: no [[Construct]], no new, no own .prototype.
User.prototype.constructor -> User; inherited/writable, not a type test.
Read searches outward. An own key shadows the same inherited key.
Assignment usually creates/updates own data, but an inherited setter may run.
Inherited non-writable data can reject assignment; defineProperty defines own.
is proto anywhere in x's chain?
Cross-realm constructors and Symbol.hasInstance can break naive instanceof tests.
Object.setPrototypeOf / __proto__ (legacy): changing a live chain is slow and fragile.
Class is prototype syntax. Prefer composition when an is-a chain adds friction.
defineProperty omitted flags default false. Rejected strict writes throw.
* shallow: nested objects stay mutable; accessor setters may still act.
7 | Proxy intercepts object operations; Reflect forwards their default semantics
Use for validation, virtualization or membranes when interception is required; keep traps minimal and forward with Reflect.

svg.text: invocation -> receiver -> own key -> prototype chain -> descriptor -> trap / invariant
